messages.author: 8b391b05c607d843
messages.subject: Spatio-temporal model on a graph
parts:
Hello,

I am new to INLA and I am wondering if I can use it for my project.
I have hourly aggregated loop detector data from around 240 stations that count cars and I have the corresponding road network graph. I'd like to model the detector counts using spatial and temporal effects.
I am unsure of how to combine the bym/besag and seasonal latent models, as every detector station has its own seasonal behavior and the model needs to describe all of those.

Do I have to put the different detector counts in a response vector for the seasonal model?That would prevent me (I think) from using the bym model, which I have used successfully by simply putting my data as count,location.

If the data wasn't bound to the road network graph, this could be solved by an SPDE model, I suppose.
Are there other ways of achieving a spatio-temporal model on a graph?

I am looking forward to any suggestions / responses!

Thank you very much!

Regards,
Thierry

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatio-temporal model on a graph
parts:
Hi,

How to do it depends on the _kind_ of seasonal model you need.
If the seasonal effects are allowed to be independent, you might be able to
use something like

f(location, model="bym") + f(hourindex, model="somecyclicalmodel", replicate=dayindex)

with some additional constraints to make it identifiable.
If the seasonal effects need to be coupled with the bym model, something like

f(location, model="bym", group=hourindex, 
  control.group=list(model="somecyclicalmodel"))

would be needed instead.
In both cases, "somecyclicalmodel" would be whatever your seasonal model should be (but only some models are supported by the "group" feature), e.g. "generic0", with precision matrix for a cyclic RW1 or RW2 model, or perhaps as simple as "iid"; as this is a problem-specific modelling choice, it's hard to give very specific advice for that. (I'm not sure what the "seasonal" latent model should be interpreted as, but suspect that it is not the type of model you want.)

All of the above assumed that the only temporal part of the model would be the seasonal effects.  It may become more complicated if you need a full spatio-temporal model with interactions between all space and time components.

Finn L
